analysis: The method writeEntry takes an InputStream and a ZipOutputStream. It creates a non-null byte array of size 1024 and repeatedly calls inputStream.read(bytes) to read data, then writes the read bytes to the zipStream. The read method is declared to throw IOException and NullPointerException according to its javadoc. In this context, the byte array `bytes` is explicitly initialized with `new byte[1024]`, so it is guaranteed to be non-null. Therefore, the condition for NullPointerException (b is null) is avoided. answer: NullPointerException: avoided (the buffer is non-null). IOException: not avoided (the code does not prevent the conditions that cause it, such as a closed stream or other I/O errors).
remark: IOException can be triggered if the inputStream is closed before or during the read operation, if the underlying I/O resource fails (e.g., network error, file system error), or if the first byte cannot be read for any reason other than the end of the stream.
